description.value:
A message block that states what happened and, when it matters, interrupts to
say so.

The alert supplies the severity, the layout and the announcement; the caller
supplies the words, and any icon or actions, through slots. There is no
built-in icon set, following `ss-icon`, which is also a slot.

description.value:
Overlaps a set of avatars into one stack, with an optional count for the ones
it does not show.

The stack is a single unit to assistive technology: the avatars themselves are
hidden from it and the group carries one name, because hearing eight names in
a row conveys less than "8 collaborators" when the individual identities are
not actionable here.

Rendered into a shadow root so that `::slotted` can lay the avatars out. A
scoped stylesheet cannot: Stencil marks only the elements a component renders
itself with its scope class, never the children the caller slots in, so
`.ss-avatar-group ss-avatar { … }` would match nothing.

attributes.name: inline-styles

description.value:
The trail of pages leading to the one being read.

The trail owns the separator, the sizing and which step is the current page;
each step draws its own separator because CSS cannot put one between slotted
children. The last step is marked as current, so a reader is told where they
are rather than being offered a link to where they already are.

attributes.name: accessibility-label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the trail, so a page with two of them stays navigable.

attributes.name: inline-styles
attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the rendered navigation element.

attributes.name: separator
attributes.description: Character drawn between steps.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size shared by every step.

attributes.name: x-id
attributes.description: Id applied to the rendered navigation element.

description.value:
One step in a breadcrumb trail.

It exists because a separator cannot be drawn between slotted children: CSS
inside a shadow root cannot reach them, a scoped stylesheet does not apply to
them, and `::slotted` takes no pseudo-element. So each step draws its own,
and the trail tells it whether it is the last one — the same coordination the
rest of this library uses.

The last step is the page the reader is already on, so it is text rather than
a link, and carries `aria-current="page"`.

attributes.name: href
attributes.description: Where this step leads. Omitted, or on the last step, it renders as plain text.

attributes.name: inline-styles
attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the rendered element.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Step text, used when no slot content is provided.

attributes.name: last
attributes.description: Whether this is the last step. Set by `ss-breadcrumb`; it decides the separator and aria-current.

attributes.name: separator
attributes.description: Separator drawn after this step. Set by `ss-breadcrumb`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the step. Set by `ss-breadcrumb`.

action that can be sent twice, so it skips the post-click disable: focus
handed back to it on close would otherwise land on a disabled control and
be lost.

description.value:
Presents a set of related actions as one group: shared sizing and styling in
one place, and an accessible name for the set.

With `attached`, the buttons become one segmented control. The seam is made
by telling each button which of its corners meet a neighbour, through `join`,
because `ss-button` renders into its own shadow root and no wrapper can reach
a border radius in there. Attaching applies to a horizontal row: a vertical
group would need to flatten block corners, which `join` does not describe.

attributes.name: accessibility-label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the set of actions.

attributes.name: attached
attributes.description: Joins the buttons into one segmented control. Horizontal groups only.

attributes.description: Disables every button in the group.

attributes.name: full-width

attributes.name: inline-styles

attributes.description: Lays the actions out in a row, or stacks them.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size shared by every button.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Colour variant shared by every button.

attributes.name: x-id
attributes.description: Id applied to the rendered container.

description.value:
A surface that groups related content, with optional media, header and footer
regions around it.

It is layout only: no elevation logic, no click behaviour and no events. A
card that should act as a link or a button holds one in its content, so the
accessible role stays on the element that actually has it; a clickable
container would have to invent the keyboard and role semantics that
`ss-button` and `ss-link` already provide.

Each region collapses when nothing is slotted into it, so an unused header
leaves no gap and draws no divider.

attributes.description: Expands the card to the full width of its container.

attributes.name: inline-styles

description.value:
Presents N `ss-checkbox` children as one `string[]` value and one change
event, with group semantics and an optional select-all master.

Membership is by value: a checkbox with no `value` cannot be a member and is
left uncoordinated, and two checkboxes sharing a value toggle together,
because the aggregate holds values rather than element identities.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables every checkbox in the group, including the master.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Error text, used when no error slot content is provided; shown only while invalid.

attributes.name: helper-text
attributes.description: Helper text, used when no helper slot content is provided.

attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the container.

attributes.name: invalid
attributes.description: Marks the group invalid: reveals the error message and sets aria-invalid.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Group label, used when no label slot content is provided.

attributes.description: Native name shared by every checkbox, for form submission.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Stacks the choices, or lays them out in a row.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description:
Requires at least one selection. HTML has no native "one of this set", so
the group expresses it with the only construct that does: while nothing is
selected the first checkbox is `required`, which makes the form invalid,
and the moment anything is selected that requirement is lifted. Only one
checkbox is ever announced as required, and checking any of them satisfies
the group rather than that particular choice.

property, following `ss-select.value`; no comma-separated form is accepted.

description.value:
A button that opens a list of actions.

It follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern, because that is what a screen
reader announces a `menu` as and what its users will press: the menu takes
focus when it opens; arrows move through the items and wrap; Home and End
jump to the ends; a typed letter moves to the next item starting with it;
Enter or Space picks one. Picking an item, or Escape, closes the menu and
hands focus back to the button. Tab closes it and lets focus move on — the
items are not tab stops, so a menu costs one stop in the page's tab order
however long it is.

A menu is for actions. For a value a form submits, use `ss-select`.

attributes.name: accessibility-label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the menu. Defaults to the trigger's label, which is what the reader just pressed.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Alignment along the trigger's edge: start, center or end. A menu reads best hanging from the start.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the dropdown; the menu stays closed and the trigger does nothing.

attributes.name: inline-styles
attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the menu.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the menu is showing. Updated on interaction, and reflected.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: Side of the trigger to open on. Moves to the opposite side when there is no room.

attributes.name: x-id
attributes.description: Id applied to the menu.

description.value:
One action in an `ss-dropdown` menu.

The item is the host itself: `role="menuitem"` and the roving focus both sit
on the element the caller wrote, so each item is a direct child of the menu
in the accessibility tree and the menu can move focus by calling `focus()`
on it. It is never a tab stop — the menu moves focus between items.

It does nothing on its own. The menu listens for the press and reports the
item's value, so a set of items needs one listener, not one per item.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the item; it is skipped by the arrow keys and cannot be picked.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Item text, used when no slot content is provided. Also what typing a letter matches against.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Value reported by the menu when this item is picked. Defaults to the label, then the text.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual treatment. `destructive` marks an action that removes something.

description.value:
Associates one form control with its label, helper text and error message,
generating the ids and coordinating the state that a consumer would otherwise
repeat on both the label and the control.

The control is supplied through the default slot and stays owned by the
caller: the field never touches its value, type, placeholder or appearance.
It sets only what association requires — the id the label points at, the
description reference, and the `required`/`disabled`/`invalid` state it was
given. State the field was not given is left as the caller set it on the
control; the field only clears what it applied itself.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the field: attenuates the label and disables the control.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Error text, used when no error slot content is provided; shown only while invalid.

attributes.name: helper-text
attributes.description: Helper text, used when no helper slot content is provided.

attributes.name: inline-styles
attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the container.

attributes.name: invalid
attributes.description: Marks the field invalid: reveals the error message and sets the control's invalid state.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Label text, used when no label slot content is provided.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Places the label above the control, or beside it.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description: Marks the field required: adds the label marker and sets the control's required state.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the label; helper and error text follow one step below it.

attributes.description: Id of the container; also the seed for the generated control and message ids.

Flattens the corners on the side that meets a neighbour, so a group can

description.value:
Joins a control to the addons beside it — a currency symbol, a unit, a button
— so the set reads as one field.

The seam is made by telling the control which of its corners meet a
neighbour, through `join`, rather than by styling it: `ss-input` renders into
its own shadow root, and no wrapper can reach a border radius in there. That
is also why the addon, not the control, is what this component draws.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the control.

attributes.name: inline-styles

description.value:
A dialog that takes over the page until it is answered.

It is the first consumer of the overlay utilities, and it is what proves
them: the focus trap and the dismissal behaviour are only really testable
through something that mounts them in a browser.

Rendered scoped rather than shadow so the trap can see the caller's content.
Focus order is a property of the composed tree, and a light-DOM query inside
a shadow root would find only what the dialog itself renders — a dialog full
of the caller's controls would look empty and trap focus on nothing.

attributes.name: accessibility-label
attributes.description: Accessible name, for a dialog with no visible heading.

attributes.name: close-on-backdrop
attributes.description: Pressing the backdrop closes the dialog.

attributes.name: close-on-escape
attributes.description: Escape closes the dialog.

attributes.name: dismiss-label
attributes.description: Accessible label for the close button.

attributes.name: dismissible
attributes.description: Renders a close button in the header.

attributes.name: heading
attributes.description: Heading text, used when no header slot content is provided.

attributes.name: inline-styles
attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the dialog element.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the dialog is showing. Updated when it is dismissed, and reflected.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Width of the dialog.

attributes.name: x-id
attributes.description: Id applied to the dialog element.

description.value:
Page navigation for a list that does not fit on one screen.

Unlike the other molecules this one is driven by props rather than slots: a
page range is data, not content, and the pages between the ends are computed
from `page` and `total`. Every rendered page is a real button, so keyboard
and screen-reader users move through the list the same way they move through
any other row of controls.

The component reports the page the reader asked for and updates its own
`page`; fetching the rows for it stays with the consumer.

attributes.name: accessibility-label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the navigation region, so a page with two of them stays distinguishable.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the whole control.

attributes.name: inline-styles
attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the container.

attributes.name: next-label
attributes.description: Label for the next-page control.

attributes.name: page
attributes.description: The page currently shown, counting from one. Updated on interaction and reflected.

attributes.name: previous-label
attributes.description: Label for the previous-page control.

attributes.name: sibling-count
attributes.description: How many pages to show either side of the current one before collapsing into a gap.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size shared by every control.

attributes.name: total
attributes.description: How many pages there are in total.

attributes.name: x-id
attributes.description: Id of the container; also included in event details.

description.value:
Content anchored to a trigger, which the reader opens, uses and puts away
without losing the page.

Where `ss-modal` takes the page over, a popover sits beside it: no backdrop
and no focus trap. Focus goes into the panel when it opens, because that is
where the reader asked to go. Closing it with Escape sends focus back to the
trigger; closing it by pressing or tabbing somewhere else leaves focus where
the reader put it.

Rendered scoped for the same reason as the modal: finding the first control
to focus, and telling whether focus has left, both need to see the caller's
content, which a shadow root would hide.

attributes.name: accessibility-label
attributes.description: Accessible name, for a panel with no visible heading.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Alignment along the trigger's edge: start, center or end.

attributes.name: close-on-escape
attributes.description: Escape closes the panel.

attributes.name: close-on-outside
attributes.description: Pressing outside the popover closes the panel.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the popover; it stays closed and the trigger does nothing.

attributes.name: heading
attributes.description: Heading shown at the top of the panel, which also names it.

attributes.name: inline-styles
attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the panel.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the panel is showing. Updated on interaction, and reflected.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: Side of the trigger to open on: top, right, bottom or left. Moves to the opposite side when there is no room.

attributes.name: x-id
attributes.description: Id applied to the panel.

attributes.name: checked
attributes.description: Whether this radio is the selected one; updated on user interaction and reflected as an attribute.

attributes.name: described-by
attributes.description: Id of the element that describes the radio, set as aria-describedby.

attributes.name: disabled

description.value:
Presents N `ss-radio` children as one selected value, one change event and
one set of group semantics, replacing the shared `name` a consumer would
otherwise repeat on every radio without ever gaining a group role, a group
label or an aggregate value.

The radios keep their own native input, styling and focus behaviour: arrow-key
navigation comes from the browser, because same-name radios in one tree
already do it. The group adds the name, the selected value, the accessible
grouping and the messages.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description:
Native name shared by every radio in the group — the thing that makes the
browser treat them as one group. Left unset, the group generates one, so a
group always works; a name is only needed to submit under a chosen key.

It stays optional because a mandatory prop would make every custom element
require it wherever a dynamic tag resolves against the generated JSX types.

description.value:
Rendered scoped rather than shadow because the description has to reach the
trigger. A tooltip's whole job is to describe the thing it points at, and
`aria-describedby` is an IDREF: with the content inside a shadow root, the
reference never resolved and the trigger was announced with no description
at all — correct-looking markup, nothing reaching the user.

attributes.description: Tooltip text rendered when no default slot content is provided.

attributes.description: Disables the tooltip; it stays closed and ignores interactions.

attributes.description: Whether the tooltip is open; updated by hover and click interactions and reflected as an attribute.

attributes.name: trigger
attributes.description: Interaction that toggles the tooltip: hover (also focus), click, or manual (controlled through open).

attributes.description: Id applied to the root element; also included in the ssOpenChange detail.

attributes.description: Font size. Defaults to the level-based size when level is set, md otherwise.

attributes.description: Font weight. Defaults to bold when level is set, regular otherwise.

attributes.name: inline-styles
attributes.description: Inline CSS styles applied to the rendered element.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description:
Heading level (1–6). Sets the rendered tag to h{level} and applies
display font, bold weight, tight line-height, and a size scaled to the
level. All defaults are overridable via the individual props.

attributes.name: line-height
attributes.description: Line height. Defaults to tight when level is set, normal otherwise.

attributes.name: transform
attributes.description: Text transform, for example uppercase.

attributes.description: Truncates overflowing text with an ellipsis on a single line.

attributes.description: Id applied to the rendered element.
